####Reproducibility####

```{r}
# Reproducabilty of control measurments -> create dataframe for analysis of the replicates
ctrl_correlations <- data.frame(
  fraction = character(),
  ctrl1_vs_ctrl2 = numeric(),
  ctrl1_vs_ctrl3 = numeric(),
  ctrl2_vs_ctrl3 = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# loop over all fractions
for (i in 0:24) {
  start_col <- 2 + i * 3 
  end_col <- start_col + 2
  ctrl_data <- df_ctrl[, start_col:end_col]
  colnames(ctrl_data) <- c("ctrl1", "ctrl2", "ctrl3")
  cor_matrix <- cor(ctrl_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
  ctrl_correlations <- rbind(ctrl_correlations, data.frame(
    fraction = paste0("fraction", i + 1),
    ctrl1_vs_ctrl2 = cor_matrix["ctrl1", "ctrl2"],
    ctrl1_vs_ctrl3 = cor_matrix["ctrl1", "ctrl3"],
    ctrl2_vs_ctrl3 = cor_matrix["ctrl2", "ctrl3"]
  ))
}

# show result
print(ctrl_correlations)
plot(ctrl_correlations) 
```

####Normalization###

```{r}
# function to compute mean columnwise (except Protein_Name)
compute_column_means <- function(df) {
  # select numeric columns (except Protein_Name)
  numeric_data <- df[, sapply(df, is.numeric)]
  
  # calculate mean coulmnwise
  col_means <- colMeans(numeric_data, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  return(col_means)
}

#apply to our data
ctrl_means <- compute_column_means(df_ctrl)
rnase_means <- compute_column_means(df_rnase)


# save means as dataframes
ctrl_means_df <- data.frame(Sample = names(ctrl_means), Mean = as.numeric(ctrl_means))
rnase_means_df <- data.frame(Sample = names(rnase_means), Mean = as.numeric(rnase_means))

#depict results
head(ctrl_means_df)
head(rnase_means_df)

#check whether there are means == 0 (to calculate normalization factor: mean are denominator -> would create NAs if mean were 0)
sum(ctrl_means_df[, 2] == 0)
sum(rnase_means_df[, 2]==0)

```

```{r}
# create function to calculate the mean of the two most similar replicates (out of three replicates)
mean_of_closest_pair <- function(x) {
  combs <- combn(x, 2)                          # all pairwise combinations
  diffs <- abs(combs[1, ] - combs[2, ])         # calculates the absolute distance
  min_idx <- which.min(diffs)                   # indices of minimal distance replicates
  mean(combs[, min_idx])                        # mean of the most similar pair
}

# alter function so it will be applied to three values at a time moving fractionwise
process_blocks <- function(values_vector) {
  n_blocks <- length(values_vector) / 3         # number of fractions
  result <- numeric(n_blocks)
  
  for (i in 1:n_blocks) {
    block <- values_vector[((i - 1) * 3 + 1):(i * 3)] #values vector contains the three values of the replicates for each fraction
    result[i] <- mean_of_closest_pair(block)
  }
  
  return(result)
}

# extract values from the dataframe 
control_values <- ctrl_means_df$Mean    
rnase_values   <- rnase_means_df$Mean

# apply to our data
control_means <- process_blocks(control_values)
rnase_means   <- process_blocks(rnase_values)

# save result as dataframe
closest_means_ctrl <- data.frame(
  Fraktion = paste0("Fraction", 1:length(control_means)),  
  Control_most_similar_pair_mean  = control_means
)

closest_means_rnase <- data.frame(
  Fraktion = paste0("Fraction", 1:length(control_means)),  
  RNase_most_similar_pair_mean = rnase_means)

# depict result
print(closest_means_ctrl)
print(closest_means_rnase)

```

```{r}
n_fractions <- 25
n_replicates <- 3

# ctrl_means_df und rnase_means_df enthalten alle Replikat-Mittelwerte in einer Spalte, z.B. 'Means'
# ctrl_final_means_df und rnase_final_means_df enthalten je einen Mittelwert pro Fraktion in 'FinalMean'

# create matrix for replicates of each fraction (25x3)
ctrl_mat <- matrix(ctrl_means_df$Mean, nrow = n_fractions, ncol = n_replicates, byrow = TRUE)
rnase_mat <- matrix(rnase_means_df$Mean, nrow = n_fractions, ncol = n_replicates, byrow = TRUE)

# initialize normalization matrixes
norm_ctrl_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_fractions, ncol = n_replicates)
norm_rnase_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_fractions, ncol = n_replicates)

# loop over all fractions
for (r in 1:n_fractions) {
  control_values <- ctrl_mat[r, ]  # 3 replicates Control
  rnase_values <- rnase_mat[r, ]   # 3 replicates RNase
  
  # FinalMean from Ctrl and RNAse dataframe
  mean_control <- closest_means_ctrl[r, 2]
  mean_rnase <- closest_means_rnase[r, 2]
  
  # check if only one value per fraction
  if(length(mean_control) != 1 | length(mean_rnase) != 1) {
    stop(paste("Mehr oder weniger als ein FinalMean für Fraktion", r))
  }
  
  # calculate normalization factors
  norm_ctrl_mat[r, ] <- mean_control / control_values
  norm_rnase_mat[r, ] <- mean_rnase / rnase_values
}

#depict results
head(norm_ctrl_mat)
head(norm_rnase_mat)

#check if any NAs were created
sum(is.na(norm_ctrl_mat))
sum(is.na(norm_rnase_mat))
```

```{r}

normalize_df <- function(df, norm_mat) {
  # extract numeric data (not "Protein_Name")
  data_mat <- as.matrix(df[, -1])
  
  # check dimensions
  n_blocks <- nrow(norm_mat)
  cols_per_block <- ncol(norm_mat)
  
  # blockwise normalization: Normierungsmatrix wird spaltenweise durchlaufen und in dieser Reihenfolge auf die Spalten der Originaldaten angewendet
  for (i in 1:n_blocks) {
    for (j in 1:cols_per_block) {
      col_index <- (i - 1) * cols_per_block + j
      data_mat[, col_index] <- data_mat[, col_index] * norm_mat[i, j]
    }
  }
  
  # create dataframe as result
  result_df <- cbind(Protein_Name = df$Protein_Name, as.data.frame(data_mat))
  return(result_df)
}

# apply to our data
normed_ctrl_df  <- normalize_df(df_ctrl, norm_ctrl_mat)
normed_rnase_df <- normalize_df(df_rnase, norm_rnase_mat)

# depict results
head(normed_ctrl_df)
head(normed_rnase_df)


```


```{r}
# Mean filter function for a row (preserving first and last value)
smooth_and_reorder <- function(df, n_fractions = 25, n_replicates = 3) {
  proteins <- df[, 1]
  
  smoothed_reps <- lapply(1:n_replicates, function(rep) {
    cols <- seq(1 + rep, 1 + rep + (n_fractions - 1) * 3, by = 3)
    rep_data <- df[, cols]
    
    smoothed_data <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(rep_data), ncol = n_fractions)
    smoothed_data[, 1] <- rep_data[, 1]
    smoothed_data[, n_fractions] <- rep_data[, n_fractions]
    
    for (i in 2:(n_fractions - 1)) {
      smoothed_data[, i] <- rowMeans(rep_data[, (i - 1):(i + 1)], na.rm = TRUE)
    }
    
    smoothed_df <- as.data.frame(smoothed_data)
    colnames(smoothed_df) <- paste0("Fraction", 1:n_fractions, "_Rep", rep)
    smoothed_df
  })
  
  combined_df <- do.call(cbind, smoothed_reps)
  
  # sort columns: first all replicates of first fraction, then fraction 2, etc.
  sorted_cols <- unlist(lapply(1:n_fractions, function(frac) {
    paste0("Fraction", frac, "_Rep", 1:n_replicates)
  }))
  
  final_df <- cbind(Protein = proteins, combined_df[, sorted_cols])
  return(final_df)
}

# apply to our data
final_smoothed_ctrl <- smooth_and_reorder(normed_ctrl_df)
final_smoothed_rnase <- smooth_and_reorder(normed_rnase_df)

# depict result
head(final_smoothed_ctrl)
head(final_smoothed_rnase)

#check if any NAs were created
sum(is.na(final_smoothed_ctrl))
sum(is.na(final_smoothed_rnase))

```

```{r}
# check for any rows with rowSum == 0 (per replicate)
check_zero_replicates_detailed <- function(df) {
  # Remove first column (protein names)
  data_only <- df[, -1]
  protein_names <- df[, 1]
  
  # Initialize lists to store results
  zero_count <- integer(nrow(data_only))
  zero_replicates <- character(nrow(data_only))
  
  # Loop through each row (protein)
  for (i in 1:nrow(data_only)) {
    affected_reps <- c()  # Temporary holder for replicate names
    
    for (rep in 1:3) {
      # Select columns for this replicate across all fractions
      replicate_indices <- seq(from = rep, to = ncol(data_only), by = 3)
      
      # Calculate sum for this replicate
      rep_sum <- sum(data_only[i, replicate_indices])
      
      # If sum is zero, store the replicate name
      if (rep_sum == 0) {
        affected_reps <- c(affected_reps, paste0("Replicate", rep))
      }
    }
    
    # Store number of zero replicates and their names
    zero_count[i] <- length(affected_reps)
    zero_replicates[i] <- if (length(affected_reps) > 0) paste(affected_reps, collapse = ", ") else NA
  }
  
  # Create final summary data frame
  summary_df <- data.frame(
    Protein = protein_names,
    Zero_Replicate_Count = zero_count,
    Affected_Replicates = zero_replicates,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Optional: filter to only those with at least one zero replicate
  summary_df <- summary_df[summary_df$Zero_Replicate_Count > 0, ]
  
  return(summary_df)
}

# Run for control
ctrl_zero_summary <- check_zero_replicates_detailed(final_smoothed_ctrl)

# Run for RNase
rnase_zero_summary <- check_zero_replicates_detailed(final_smoothed_rnase)

# View examples
head(ctrl_zero_summary)
head(rnase_zero_summary)


```


```{r}
#normalize total amount per replicate to 100%
calc_fraction_percentages <- function(df, zero_info, n_fractions = 25, n_replicates = 3) {
  proteins <- df[, 1]
  percent_reps <- list()
  
  for (rep in 1:n_replicates) {
    # Select replicate columns for all fractions (e.g., Rep1 of all fractions)
    cols <- seq(1 + rep, 1 + rep + (n_fractions - 1) * 3, by = 3)
    rep_data <- as.matrix(df[, cols])
    
    # Get logical vector: TRUE if replicate sum == 0 (should NOT be normalized)
    rep_name <- paste0("Replicate", rep)
    skip_replicate <- zero_info[[rep_name]] == TRUE  # original values are kept

    
    # Calculate row sums
    row_sums <- rowSums(rep_data, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Normalize only where rowSum != 0
    percent_data <- rep_data  # start with original values
    
    # Normalize where allowed (i.e., rowSum != 0)
    normalize_rows <- !skip_replicate
    percent_data[normalize_rows, ] <- sweep(
      rep_data[normalize_rows, ],
      1,
      row_sums[normalize_rows],
      FUN = "/"
    ) * 100
    
    # Create dataframe and set column names
    percent_df <- as.data.frame(percent_data)
    colnames(percent_df) <- paste0("Fraction", 1:n_fractions, "_Rep", rep)
    percent_reps[[rep]] <- percent_df
  }
  
  # Combine all replicate dataframes
  combined_percent_df <- do.call(cbind, percent_reps)
  
  # Reorder columns: Fraction1_Rep1, Fraction1_Rep2, Fraction1_Rep3, etc.
  sorted_cols <- unlist(lapply(1:n_fractions, function(frac) {
    paste0("Fraction", frac, "_Rep", 1:n_replicates)
  }))
  
  final_percent_df <- cbind(Protein = proteins, combined_percent_df[, sorted_cols])
  return(final_percent_df)
}


# Run the replicate-zero check
ctrl_zero_info <- check_zero_replicates_detailed(final_smoothed_ctrl)
rnase_zero_info <- check_zero_replicates_detailed(final_smoothed_rnase)

# Run the adjusted percentage calculation
percent_ctrl_df <- calc_fraction_percentages(final_smoothed_ctrl, ctrl_zero_info)
percent_rnase_df <- calc_fraction_percentages(final_smoothed_rnase, rnase_zero_info)

# View results
head(percent_ctrl_df)
head(percent_rnase_df)

#check for NAs
sum(is.na(percent_ctrl_df))
sum(is.na(percent_rnase_df))
```

```{r}
calculate_mean_per_fraction <- function(df, n_fractions = 25, n_replicates = 3) {
  proteins <- df[, 1]  # Protein-Names
  data_only <- df[, -1]  # only numeric values

  mean_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(data_only), ncol = n_fractions)

  for (f in 1:n_fractions) {
    # columns for fraction f (3 replicates each)
    cols <- ((f - 1) * n_replicates + 1):(f * n_replicates)
    mean_matrix[, f] <- rowMeans(data_only[, cols], na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  # save result as dataframe
  mean_df <- as.data.frame(mean_matrix)
  colnames(mean_df) <- paste0("Fraction", 1:n_fractions)
  final_df <- cbind(Protein = proteins, mean_df)

  return(final_df)
}

#apply to our data
mean_ctrl_df <- calculate_mean_per_fraction(percent_ctrl_df)
mean_rnase_df <- calculate_mean_per_fraction(percent_rnase_df)

# depict results
head(mean_ctrl_df)
head(mean_rnase_df)

#check if NAs were created
sum(is.na(mean_ctrl_df))
sum(is.na(mean_rnase_df))
```

```{r}
# normalization of amount of protein to equal 100%

calculate_fraction_percentages <- function(mean_df) {
  proteins <- mean_df[, 1]
  data_only <- mean_df[, -1]
  
  # calculate row sum (sum across all fractions for each protein)
  row_totals <- rowSums(data_only, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # transform amount into percent
  percent_matrix <- sweep(data_only, 1, row_totals, FUN = "/") * 100
  
  # combine result to a dataframe
  percent_df <- cbind(Protein = proteins, as.data.frame(percent_matrix))
  colnames(percent_df) <- colnames(mean_df)
  
  return(percent_df)
}


# apply to our data
normalized_ctrl_df  <- calculate_fraction_percentages(mean_ctrl_df)
normalized_rnase_df <- calculate_fraction_percentages(mean_rnase_df)

# depict result
head(normalized_ctrl_df)
head(normalized_rnase_df)

#check if any NAs were created
sum(is.na(normalized_ctrl_df))
sum(is.na(normalized_rnase_df))


```

##Visualization

```{r}
# Protein auswählen
protein_id <- "KIF2A_HUMAN"

# Zeile finden, die dem Protein entspricht
protein_row <- which(normalized_ctrl_df[, 1] == protein_id)

# Normierte Intensitäten extrahieren
intensities_ctrl <- as.numeric(normalized_ctrl_df[protein_row, 2:26])
intensities_rnase <- as.numeric(normalized_rnase_df[protein_row, 2:26])
fraktionen <- 1:25

# Plot vorbereiten (ohne automatische x-Achse)
plot(fraktionen, intensities_ctrl, type = "n",
     xlab = "Fraktion (1–25)", ylab = "Proteinmenge",
     main = paste("Vergleich: Kontrolle vs. RNase für", protein_id),
     ylim = c(0, max(c(intensities_ctrl, intensities_rnase)) * 1.1),
     xaxt = "n")  # <- x-Achse deaktivieren

# Eigene x-Achse: Alle Fraktionen anzeigen
axis(1, at = 1:25)

# Gitterlinien
grid(col = "lightgray", lty = "dotted")

# Kontrolle: Lavendel-Ton
ctrl_fill_color <- rgb(0.7, 0.6, 1, 0.3)
ctrl_line_color <- rgb(0.7, 0.6, 1)

polygon(c(fraktionen, rev(fraktionen)),
        c(rep(0, length(fraktionen)), rev(intensities_ctrl)),
        col = ctrl_fill_color, border = NA)
lines(fraktionen, intensities_ctrl, col = ctrl_line_color, lwd = 2)

# RNase: Blau-Ton
rnase_fill_color <- rgb(0, 1, 1, 0.3)
rnase_line_color <- rgb(0, 1, 1)

polygon(c(fraktionen, rev(fraktionen)),
        c(rep(0, length(fraktionen)), rev(intensities_rnase)),
        col = rnase_fill_color, border = NA)
lines(fraktionen, intensities_rnase, col = rnase_line_color, lwd = 2)

# Legende
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Kontrolle", "RNase"),
       col = c(ctrl_line_color, rnase_line_color),
       lwd = 2,
       bg = "white")


```

###Batch Effect###

##CONTROL
##boxplot
```{r}
# 1. Matrix mit Expressionswerten extrahieren (ohne Protein-Spalte)
ctrl_expr_matrix <- as.matrix(final_smoothed_ctrl[, -1])  

# 2. Sample-Namen extrahieren
sample_names <- colnames(ctrl_expr_matrix)

# 3. Batch-Labels aus Sample-Namen ziehen (Rep1, Rep2, Rep3)
batch <- sub(".*_(Rep\\d)", "\\1", sample_names)
batch <- factor(batch, levels = c("Rep1", "Rep2", "Rep3"))

# 4. Farben zuordnen
batch_colors <- c("Rep1" = "red", "Rep2" = "green", "Rep3" = "blue")
colors <- batch_colors[as.character(batch)]

# 5. Boxplot zeichnen
boxplot(ctrl_expr_matrix,
        main = "Expression nach Sample (Batch gefärbt)",
        ylab = "Expression",
        xlab = "Samples",
        las = 2,                      # X-Achse: senkrechte Labels
        col = colors,
        outline = FALSE,
        cex.axis = 0.6)              # kleinere Achsenbeschriftung

# 6. Legende hinzufügen
legend("topright",
       legend = names(batch_colors),
       fill = batch_colors,
       title = "Batch")
```

```{r}


library(limma)

# 1. Matrix mit Expressionswerten extrahieren (ohne Protein-Spalte)
ctrl_expr_matrix <- as.matrix(final_smoothed_ctrl[, -1])  

# 2. Sample-Namen extrahieren
sample_names <- colnames(ctrl_expr_matrix)

# 3. Batch-Labels aus Sample-Namen ziehen (Rep1, Rep2, Rep3)
batch <- sub(".*_(Rep\\d)", "\\1", sample_names)
batch <- factor(batch, levels = c("Rep1", "Rep2", "Rep3"))

# 4. Log2-Transformation (falls nötig, empfohlen wegen Skalenproblem)
ctrl_expr_matrix_log <- log2(ctrl_expr_matrix + 1)

# 5. Batch-Korrektur mit limma
L_ctrl_expr_corrected <- removeBatchEffect(ctrl_expr_matrix_log, batch = batch)



# 5. Boxplot zeichnen vor korrektur 
boxplot(ctrl_expr_matrix_log,
        main = "Expression vor Korrektur (Batch gefärbt)",
        ylab = "Expression",
        xlab = "Samples",
        las = 2,                      # X-Achse: senkrechte Labels
        col = colors,
        outline = FALSE,
        cex.axis = 0.6)              # kleinere Achsenbeschriftung

# Boxplot nach Korrektur 
boxplot(L_ctrl_expr_corrected,
        main = "Expression nach Korrektur (Batch gefärbt)",
        ylab = "Expression",
        xlab = "Samples",
        las = 2,                      # X-Achse: senkrechte Labels
        col = colors,
        outline = FALSE,
        cex.axis = 0.6)              # kleinere Achsenbeschriftung


# 6. Legende hinzufügen
legend_labels <- c("Batch A", "Batch B", "Batch C")
legend("topright",
       legend = legend_labels,
       fill = batch_colors,
       title = "Batch")
```


## PCA
```{r}
# PCA-Analyse vorbereiten
pca_before <- prcomp(t(ctrl_expr_matrix_log), scale. = TRUE)
pca_after  <- prcomp(t(L_ctrl_expr_corrected), scale. = TRUE)

# Batch-Zuordnung erneut für Farben
# 2. Sample-Namen extrahieren
sample_names <- colnames(ctrl_expr_matrix_log)

# 3. Batch-Labels aus Sample-Namen ziehen (Rep1, Rep2, Rep3)
batch <- sub(".*_(Rep\\d)", "\\1", sample_names)
batch <- factor(batch, levels = c("Rep1", "Rep2", "Rep3"))
# Plot nebeneinander
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# PCA vor Korrektur
plot(pca_before$x[, 1:2],
     col = rainbow(length(levels(batch)))[batch],
     pch = 19,
     main = "PCA vor Batch-Korrektur")
legend("topright", legend = levels(batch), col = rainbow(length(levels(batch))), pch = 19)

# PCA nach Korrektur
plot(pca_after$x[, 1:2],
```

##control
```{r}
install.packages("sva")

# Lade benötigte Libraries
library(sva)
library(stringr)
library(limma)

# 1) Expressionsmatrix (ohne Protein-Spalte)
ctrl_expression_matrix <- as.matrix(final_smoothed_ctrl[, -1])
rownames(ctrl_expression_matrix) <- final_smoothed_ctrl$Protein

# 2) Metadaten (sampleInfo) aus Spaltennamen erzeugen
ctrl_samples <- colnames(ctrl_expression_matrix)

# Extrahiere "Fraction" und "Replicate" Informationen aus Spaltennamen
fraction <- str_extract(ctrl_samples, "Fraction\\d+")
replicate <- str_extract(ctrl_samples, "Rep\\d+")

# sampleInfo DataFrame erstellen
C_sampleInfo <- data.frame(
  fraction = factor(fraction),
  replicate = factor(replicate)
)

# 3) Designmatrix für das Modell erstellen
mod <- model.matrix(~ fraction + replicate, data = C_sampleInfo)
mod0 <- model.matrix(~ 1, data = C_sampleInfo)  # Nullmodell ohne Prädiktoren

# 4) SVA durchführen
sva_res_ctrl <- sva(ctrl_expression_matrix, mod, mod0)

# 5) Designmatrix um die gefundenen Surrogate Variablen (SVs) erweitern
mod_sv <- cbind(mod, sva_res_ctrl$sv)

# 6) OPTIONAL: Wenn du einen bekannten Batch hast, kannst du alternativ ComBat verwenden
# Beispiel (nur wenn du 'batch' hast):
# batch <- sampleInfo$batch_variable
# expression_corrected <- ComBat(dat = expression_matrix, batch = batch, mod = mod)

# 7) Korrektur mit Surrogate Variablen durch lineare Regression (empfohlen bei unbekanntem Batch)
# Fit des linearen Modells mit Surrogate Variablen
fit <- lmFit(ctrl_expression_matrix, mod_sv)
fit <- eBayes(fit)

# Residuen extrahieren = korrigierter Datensatz ohne die erklärten Effekte (fraction + replicate + SVs)
S_corrected_expr_ctrl <- residuals(fit, ctrl_expression_matrix)

# 'corrected_expr' enthält die bereinigten Expressionswerte
```

### maxima
```{r}
##Doch Unnötig !
# IdentifY position of global maxima
# recognize peaks with diff()
find_peaks_diff <- function(x, threshold = 2) {
  n <- length(x)
  peaks <- logical(n)
  
  dx <- diff(x)
  
  # Interne Punkte prüfen: vorher steigend, danach fallend
  for (i in 2:(n-1)) {
    if (x[i] >= threshold && dx[i-1] > 0 && dx[i] < 0) {
      peaks[i] <- TRUE
    }
  }
 
  if (x[1] >= threshold && x[1] > x[2]) peaks[1] <- TRUE
  if (x[n] >= threshold && x[n] > x[n-1]) peaks[n] <- TRUE
  
  which(peaks)
}

# experimental application with a protein
process_df_peaks <- function(df, threshold = 2) {
  results <- lapply(1:nrow(df), function(i) {
    intensities <- as.numeric(df[i, 2:26])
    protein <- df[i, 1]
    peaks <- find_peaks_diff(intensities, threshold)
    list(Protein = protein, Peaks = peaks)
  })
  
  # save as dataframe
  df_peaks <- data.frame(
    Protein = sapply(results, `[[`, "Protein"),
    Maxima_Positions = sapply(results, function(x) {
      if (length(x$Peaks) == 0) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        paste(x$Peaks, collapse = ",")
      }
    }),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(df_peaks)
}

# apply to our dataframe

df_peaks_CTRL <- process_df_peaks(normalized_ctrl_df, threshold = 2)
df_peaks_RNAse <- process_df_peaks(normalized_rnase_df, threshold = 2)


# depict results
head(df_peaks_CTRL)
head(df_peaks_RNAse)

```
### global maxima positions
```{r}
# Identify global maxima and their position, if present
find_global_maxima <- function(x, threshold = 2) {
  max_val <- max(x)
  if (max_val >= threshold) {
    max_positions <- which(x == max_val)
    if (length(max_positions) == 1) {
      return(max_positions)
    } else {
      middle_index <- mean(range(max_positions))
      return(middle_index)
    }
  } else {
    return(NA_real_)  
  }
}

# extract intensity of the protein concentration in each fraction
process_df_global_maxima <- function(df, threshold = 2) {
  results <- lapply(1:nrow(df), function(i) {
    intensities <- as.numeric(df[i, 2:26])
    protein <- df[i, 1]
    maxima <- find_global_maxima(intensities, threshold)
    list(Protein = protein, Global_Maximum = maxima)
  })
  
  df_maxima <- data.frame(
    Protein = sapply(results, `[[`, "Protein"),
    Global_Maximum = sapply(results, `[[`, "Global_Maximum"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(df_maxima)
}

# Apply to our dataframe
global_ctrl <- process_df_global_maxima(normalized_ctrl_df, threshold = 2)
global_rnase <- process_df_global_maxima(normalized_rnase_df, threshold = 2)

head(global_ctrl)

```

```{r}
# Robust scaling function: (x - median) / IQR
robust_scale <- function(x) {
  med <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  scaled <- (x - med) / iqr
  return(scaled)
}

# Apply robust scaling to each variable
shift_result$Shift_Distance_scaled <- robust_scale(abs(shift_result$Shift_Distance))
```

### earth mover test
```{r}
library(emdist)

# Custom function to compute 1D Earth Mover's Distance
compute_emd_1d <- function(vec1, vec2) {
  # Remove NAs
  vec1 <- as.numeric(na.omit(vec1))
  vec2 <- as.numeric(na.omit(vec2))
  
  # Ensure both vectors have the same length
  if (length(vec1) != length(vec2)) {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  # Normalize both vectors to sum to 1 (as probability distributions)
  vec1 <- vec1 / sum(vec1)
  vec2 <- vec2 / sum(vec2)
  
  # Compute cumulative distributions
  cdf1 <- cumsum(vec1)
  cdf2 <- cumsum(vec2)
  
  # EMD in 1D is the sum of absolute differences of CDFs
  emd <- sum(abs(cdf1 - cdf2))
  
  return(emd)
}

# Vector to store EMD results
emd_values <- numeric(nrow(normalized_ctrl_df))

# Loop through all proteins (rows)
for (i in 1:nrow(normalized_ctrl_df)) {
  # Extract fraction profiles (columns 2 to 26)
  vec_ctrl <- as.numeric(normalized_ctrl_df[i, 2:26])
  vec_rnase <- as.numeric(normalized_rnase_df[i, 2:26])
  
  # Compute 1D EMD
  emd_values[i] <- compute_emd_1d(vec_ctrl, vec_rnase)
}

# Add EMD results as a new column to the data frame
normalized_ctrl_df$EMD <- emd_values
normalized_rnase_df$EMD <- emd_values  # Optional, for consistency (values are the same as for Ctrl)

#EMD results can potentially range from 0 (Ctrl and RNase are identical) to 25 (Ctrl and RNase are as dissimilar as they can be)

# depict results
head(normalized_ctrl_df[, c(1, 27)])  # Show protein name and EMD
```

### center of mass test
```{r}
# center of mass
# function for calculating center of mass
center_of_mass <- function(values) {
  fracs <- seq_along(values)
  if (sum(values, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) return(NA)
  sum(fracs * values, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(values, na.rm = TRUE)
}
# function for calculating maximal possible COM shift
max_possible_com_shift <- function(values) {
  fracs <- seq_along(values)
  if (sum(values, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) return(NA)

  # create two extreme distributions
  only_first <- numeric(length(values))
  only_last  <- numeric(length(values))
  only_first[1] <- 1
  only_last[length(values)] <- 1

  # COM for extreme distributions
  com_min <- center_of_mass(only_first)
  com_max <- center_of_mass(only_last)

  # theoretical max delta
  abs(com_max - com_min)
}


# remove column with protein names
fractions_control <- normalized_ctrl_df[, 2:26]
fractions_rnase   <- normalized_rnase_df[, 2:26]

# calculate center of mass
com_control <- apply(fractions_control, 1, center_of_mass)
com_rnase   <- apply(fractions_rnase, 1, center_of_mass)

# calculate maximal possible shift for every protein
max_delta_com <- apply(fractions_control, 1, max_possible_com_shift)

# Delta and relative shift
delta_com <- com_rnase - com_control
relative_delta_com <- abs(delta_com) / max_delta_com

# define dataframe with results and difference between both treatments
center_of_mass_df <- data.frame(
  Protein     = normalized_ctrl_df[[1]],  # extract protein names from the first column
  COM_Control = com_control,
  COM_RNase   = com_rnase,
  Delta_COM   = delta_com,
  Max_Delta_COM      = max_delta_com,
  Relative_Delta_COM = relative_delta_com
)

# View first few results
head(center_of_mass_df)
```

### wilcoxon statistic: position of maxima between replicates of conditions are compared
```{r}
# determine global maxima from dataframes with still all 3 replicates in them

# prepare data
# remove protein-column
percent_ctrl <- percent_ctrl_df[, -1]
percent_rnase <- percent_rnase_df[, -1]

# define replicates as steps by 3
rep1_cols <- seq(1, ncol(percent_ctrl), by = 3)
rep2_cols <- seq(2, ncol(percent_ctrl), by = 3)
rep3_cols <- seq(3, ncol(percent_ctrl), by = 3)


# formula for extracting global maxima and their position
get_max_and_pos <- function(mat) {
  max_vals <- apply(mat, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_pos <- apply(mat, 1, function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) NA else which.max(x)
  })
  list(value = max_vals, pos = max_pos)
}

# formula for extracting position as numeric fraction value
extract_fraction_number <- function(name_vector) {
  as.numeric(sub("Fraction(\\d+)_Rep\\d+", "\\1", name_vector))
}

# apply formulas on both treatments
ctrl_r1 <- get_max_and_pos(percent_ctrl[, rep1_cols])
ctrl_r2 <- get_max_and_pos(percent_ctrl[, rep2_cols])
ctrl_r3 <- get_max_and_pos(percent_ctrl[, rep3_cols])

rnase_r1 <- get_max_and_pos(percent_rnase[, rep1_cols])
rnase_r2 <- get_max_and_pos(percent_rnase[, rep2_cols])
rnase_r3 <- get_max_and_pos(percent_rnase[, rep3_cols])

# define column names
names_r1 <- colnames(percent_ctrl)[rep1_cols]
names_r2 <- colnames(percent_ctrl)[rep2_cols]
names_r3 <- colnames(percent_ctrl)[rep3_cols]

# define protein names
protein_names <- percent_ctrl_df[, 1]

# save maxima results as dataframes
global_max_ctrl_df <- data.frame(
  Protein = protein_names,
  Max_Rep1 = ctrl_r1$value,
  Max_Rep2 = ctrl_r2$value,
  Max_Rep3 = ctrl_r3$value
)

global_max_rnase_df <- data.frame(
  Protein = protein_names,
  Max_Rep1 = rnase_r1$value,
  Max_Rep2 = rnase_r2$value,
  Max_Rep3 = rnase_r3$value
)

# save fraction position as dataframes
fraktion_pos_ctrl_df <- data.frame(
  Protein = protein_names,
  Max_Pos_Rep1 = extract_fraction_number(names_r1[ctrl_r1$pos]),
  Max_Pos_Rep2 = extract_fraction_number(names_r2[ctrl_r2$pos]),
  Max_Pos_Rep3 = extract_fraction_number(names_r3[ctrl_r3$pos])
)

fraktion_pos_rnase_df <- data.frame(
  Protein = protein_names,
  Max_Pos_Rep1 = extract_fraction_number(names_r1[rnase_r1$pos]),
  Max_Pos_Rep2 = extract_fraction_number(names_r2[rnase_r2$pos]),
  Max_Pos_Rep3 = extract_fraction_number(names_r3[rnase_r3$pos])
```

```{r}
#paired Wilxocon test to compare the global maxima positions between control und rnase
# Prepare vectors to store results
p_values <- numeric(nrow(fraktion_pos_ctrl_df))       # p-values
test_statistics <- numeric(nrow(fraktion_pos_ctrl_df))  # test statistic (W)

# Loop through each protein (each row)
for (i in 1:nrow(fraktion_pos_ctrl_df)) {
  # Extract numeric values from columns 2 to 4 for both conditions
  ctrl_values <- as.numeric(fraktion_pos_ctrl_df[i, 2:4])
  rnase_values <- as.numeric(fraktion_pos_rnase_df[i, 2:4])
  
  # Check if all paired values are identical
  if (all(ctrl_values == rnase_values)) {
    # No difference → Wilcoxon test not defined
    p_values[i] <- 1
    test_statistics[i] <- 0  # or NA, depending on your needs
  } else {
    # Run paired Wilcoxon test
    test_result <- wilcox.test(ctrl_values, rnase_values, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)
    
    # Store results
    p_values[i] <- test_result$p.value
    test_statistics[i] <- test_result$statistic
  }
}

# Combine results into a dataframe with protein names
Wilcoxon_Pos_Max <- data.frame(
  Protein = fraktion_pos_ctrl_df[[1]],
  P_value = p_values,
  Wilcoxon_statistic = test_statistics
)

# View first few results
head(Wilcoxon_Pos_Max)
```

```{r}
#  which is about 30% of all proteins, suitable for a 30/70 training-test split)

# Filter proteins with '0' in column 4 that are present in the dataset 
zero_proteins <- intersect(RNA_independent[RNA_independent[,4] == 0, 1], normalized_ctrl_df[,1])

# Filter proteins with '1' in column 4 that are present in the dataset 
one_proteins <- intersect(RNA_independent[RNA_independent[,4] == 1, 1], normalized_ctrl_df[,1])

# Count how many definite negatives we have
n_zero <- length(zero_proteins)

# Calculate how many proteins with '1' we need to sample to reach 550 total
n_fill <- 550 - n_zero

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)

# Randomly sample the required number of '1' proteins to fill the negative control set
sampled_one_proteins <- sample(one_proteins, n_fill)

# Combine the definite negatives and sampled proteins to form the final negative control set
negative_control <- c(zero_proteins, sampled_one_proteins)

# Confirm the length of the final negative control vector (should be 550)
length(negative_control)
```

```{r}
#check whether positive and negative control are reliable and whether they differ significantly 
# Vector of column indices to test
cols_to_test <- c(2,4,5,6,7,8)

# Empty list to store test results
test_results <- list()

for (col in cols_to_test) {
  # Extract the column from both dataframes
  pos_values <- df_positive_control[[col]]
  neg_values <- df_negative_control[[col]]
  
  # Perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum test (Mann-Whitney U test)
  test <- wilcox.test(pos_values, neg_values)
  
  # Store the p-value with the column name as key
  test_results[[colnames(df_positive_control)[col]]] <- test$p.value
}

# Create a data frame to display p-values
test_results_df <- data.frame(
  Column = names(test_results),
  p_value = unlist(test_results)
)

# Print the results
print(test_results_df)

```


```{r}
# 1. Add labels to the datasets
df_positive_control$label <- 1  # Positive control group labeled as 1
df_negative_control$label <- 0  # Negative control group labeled as 0

# 2. Combine the datasets and keep the relevant columns (features + label)
df_all <- rbind(
  df_positive_control[, c("EMD", "Shift_Distance_ctrl_to_rnase", "amplitude_changes", "Center_of_Mass", "Wilcoxon_statistic_Max", "Wilcoxon_statistic", "label")],
  df_negative_control[, c("EMD", "Shift_Distance_ctrl_to_rnase", "amplitude_changes", "Center_of_Mass", "Wilcoxon_statistic_Max", "Wilcoxon_statistic", "label")]
)

# 3. Fit logistic regression model with multiple predictors
logistic_model <- glm(label ~ EMD + Shift_Distance_ctrl_to_rnase + amplitude_changes + Center_of_Mass + Wilcoxon_statistic + Wilcoxon_statistic_Max,
                      data = df_all,
                      family = binomial)

# 4. Display model summary to see weights (coefficients)
summary(logistic_model)

# 5. Create a combined weighted score using coefficients
coeffs <- coef(logistic_model)[-1]  # exclude intercept
df_all$weighted_score <- rowSums(sweep(df_all[, names(coeffs)], 2, coeffs, FUN = "*"))

# 6. Boxplot of weighted scores by label
boxplot(weighted_score ~ label, data = df_all,
        names = c("Negative", "Positive"),
        xlab = "Class Label", ylab = "Weighted Score",
        main = "Distribution of Weighted Scores by Class")

```

```{r}
#apply model to our data
# 1. Calculate predicted probabilities (e.g., RNA-dependency) using the logistic model
test_scores_combined_df$probability <- predict(logistic_model, newdata = test_scores_combined_df, type = "response")

# 2. View the first few rows of the result
head(test_scores_combined_df)
```

```{r}
#calculate threshold automatically
# 1. predictions
test_scores_combined_df$predicted_prob <- predict(logistic_model, newdata = test_scores_combined_df, type = "response")

# 2. Marks for reference
test_scores_combined_df$is_negative <- test_scores_combined_df$Protein %in% df_negative_control$Protein

# 3. Evaluate thresholds 
thresholds <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.001)
fdr_values <- sapply(thresholds, function(thresh) {
  selected <- test_scores_combined_df[test_scores_combined_df$predicted_prob > thresh, ]
  if (nrow(selected) == 0) return(NA)
  
  false_positives <- sum(selected$is_negative, na.rm = TRUE)
  all_positives   <- nrow(selected)
  fdr <- false_positives / all_positives
  return(fdr)
})

# 4. Find threshold at FDR ≤ 10% 
target_fdr <- 0.10
valid_thresholds <- thresholds[which(fdr_values <= target_fdr)]
optimal_threshold <- if (length(valid_thresholds) > 0) min(valid_thresholds) else NA

cat("Threshold bei FDR ≤ 10%:", optimal_threshold, "\n")

#visualize FDR
plot(thresholds, fdr_values, type = "l", col = "lavender", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Prediction Threshold", ylab = "FDR",
     main = "FDR vs Threshold")
abline(h = 0.1, col = "violet", lty = 2)
abline(v = optimal_threshold, col = "lightgreen", lty = 2)

```

```{r}
#threshold is selected at FDR = 10%

# 2. Make predictions using the logistic model
predictions <- predict(logistic_model, newdata = test_scores_combined_df, type = "response")

# 3. Apply threshold (e.g., 0.95) to get predicted positives
selected_proteins <- test_scores_combined_df[predictions > optimal_threshold, ]
selected_proteins$is_reference <- selected_proteins$Protein %in% df_positive_control$Protein


# 4. Count how many of the selected proteins are reference proteins

#how many proteins of negative control are found at this threshold
# 1. Mark negative control proteins in the full dataset
test_scores_combined_df$is_negative <- test_scores_combined_df$Protein %in% df_negative_control$Protein

# 2. Make predictions using the existing logistic model
predictions <- predict(logistic_model, newdata = test_scores_combined_df, type = "response")

# 3. Apply threshold (z.B. gleich wie oben: 0.3899612)
selected_proteins <- test_scores_combined_df[predictions > optimal_threshold, ]

# 4. Count how many of the selected proteins are from the negative control
neg_counts <- table(selected_proteins$is_negative)
names(neg_counts) <- c("Not negative control protein (FALSE)", "Negative control protein (TRUE)")
print(neg_counts)

# Extract those negative control proteins among predicted positives
predicted_negatives <- selected_proteins[selected_proteins$is_negative, ]

# Extract predicted hits that are NOT from the negative control -> TRUE: number of proteins from negative-control that are classified as shifting from the model
predicted_non_negative <- selected_proteins[!selected_proteins$is_negative, ]
```

# 'app' panel: Protein Profile Viewer
```{r}
#macht quasi dasselbe wie der chunk obendrüber aber hat anschaulichere Eingabemöglichkeit für Protein of interest
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Protein Profile Viewer"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      textInput("protein_name", "Enter Protein Name:", ""),
      actionButton("plot_button", "Plot")
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("proteinPlot")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  observeEvent(input$plot_button, {
    protein_name <- input$protein_name
    
    if (!exists("normalized_ctrl_df") || !exists("normalized_rnase_df") || 
    !exists("test_scores_combined_df") || !exists("optimal_threshold")) {
  output$proteinPlot <- renderPlot(NULL)
  showNotification("One or more required data objects are missing.", type = "error")
  return()
}
    
    # Select columns 1 (name) and 2:26 (Fraction1 to Fraction25)
    ctrl <- normalized_ctrl_df[, c(1, 2:26)]
    rnase <- normalized_rnase_df[, c(1, 2:26)]
    
    # Filter for selected protein
    ctrl_data <- ctrl %>% filter(Protein == protein_name)
    rnase_data <- rnase %>% filter(Protein == protein_name)
    
    if (nrow(ctrl_data) == 0 | nrow(rnase_data) == 0) {
      output$proteinPlot <- renderPlot(NULL)
      showNotification("Protein not found in Control or RNase dataset.", type = "error")
      return()
    }
    
    # Label condition
    ctrl_data$Condition <- "Control"
    rnase_data$Condition <- "RNase"
    
    # Combine and reshape
    combined <- bind_rows(ctrl_data, rnase_data)
    long_df <- combined %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Fraction"),
                   names_to = "Fraction", values_to = "Intensity") %>%
      mutate(Fraction = as.numeric(gsub("Fraction", "", Fraction)))
    
    # Get model probability and RBP classification
    prob <- test_scores_combined_df$probability[test_scores_combined_df$Protein == protein_name]
    if (length(prob) == 0) prob <- NA
    classification <- ifelse(!is.na(prob) & prob > optimal_threshold, "RBP", "Non-RBP")
    
    output$proteinPlot <- renderPlot({
      ggplot(long_df, aes(x = Fraction, y = Intensity, color = Condition, fill = Condition)) +
        geom_area(alpha = 0.3, position = "identity", show.legend = FALSE) +
        geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
        scale_color_manual(values = c("Control" = "mediumpurple", "RNase" = "steelblue")) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c("Control" = "mediumpurple", "RNase" = "steelblue")) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(5, 25, by = 5), limits = c(1, 25)) +
        labs(
          title = paste("Profile for Protein:", protein_name),
          subtitle = paste0("Predicted Probability: ", round(prob, 3),
                            " | Classified as: ", classification),
          x = "Fraction",
          y = "Normalized Intensity",
          color = "Condition"
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
              panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())
    })
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

#### violinplots
```{r}
# visualize the shift/non-shift of three selected proteins as violinplot
proteins <- c("RLA1_HUMAN", "APC16_HUMAN", "CH033_HUMAN")

# Plotpreperation
n <- length(proteins)
x_positions <- seq(1, by = 1, length.out = n)

# Y-axes
all_values <- c()
for (p in proteins) {
  v1 <- as.numeric(normalized_ctrl_df[normalized_ctrl_df[[1]] == p, 2:26])
  v2 <- as.numeric(normalized_rnase_df[normalized_rnase_df[[1]] == p, 2:26])
  all_values <- c(all_values, v1, v2)
}

# Basisplot
plot(NA,
     xlim = c(0.5, n + 0.5),
     ylim = range(all_values, na.rm = TRUE),
     xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "",
     ylab = "Intensität",
     main = "Symmetrische Violinplots")

axis(1, at = x_positions, labels = proteins, las = 2)

# plot
for (i in seq_along(proteins)) {
  protein <- proteins[i]
  x <- x_positions[i]

  ctrl_vals <- as.numeric(normalized_ctrl_df[normalized_ctrl_df[[1]] == protein, 2:26])
  rnase_vals <- as.numeric(normalized_rnase_df[normalized_rnase_df[[1]] == protein, 2:26])
  
  
  if (sum(!is.na(ctrl_vals)) < 2 || sum(!is.na(rnase_vals)) < 2) {
    next
  }

  # calculate density and check validity
  dens_ctrl <- tryCatch(density(ctrl_vals, na.rm = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  dens_rnase <- tryCatch(density(rnase_vals, na.rm = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (is.null(dens_ctrl) || is.null(dens_rnase)) {
    next
  }
  
  # check length of both x- and y-vector -> have to be the same length
  if (length(dens_ctrl$x) != length(dens_ctrl$y) || length(dens_rnase$x) != length(dens_rnase$y)) {
    next
  }

  # scaling
  max_y <- max(c(dens_ctrl$y, dens_rnase$y))
  scale_factor <- 0.4 / max_y

  # Violine: Control on left
x_left  <- x - dens_ctrl$y * scale_factor
y_vals  <- dens_ctrl$x
polygon(
  x = c(x_left, rev(x_left)),
  y = c(y_vals, rev(y_vals)),
  col = "lightblue", border = "blue"
)

# Violine: RNase on right
x_right <- x + dens_rnase$y * scale_factor
y_vals2 <- dens_rnase$x
polygon(
  x = c(x_right, rev(x_right)),
  y = c(y_vals2, rev(y_vals2)),
  col = "lightpink", border="red"
)

  # add median line
  med_ctrl <- median(ctrl_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  med_rnase <- median(rnase_vals, na.rm = TRUE)

  lines(c(x - 0.2, x), rep(med_ctrl, 2), col = "blue", lty = 2)
  lines(c(x, x + 0.2), rep(med_rnase, 2), col = "red", lty = 2)
}

# add legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Control", "RNase"),
       fill = c("lightblue", "lightpink"),
       border = c("blue", "red"),
       bty="n")
```

```{r}
#Silhouette 

library(cluster)
library(factoextra)

# Deine PCA-Daten
df <- Ctrl_pca$x

# Silhouettenmittelwerte für verschiedene k berechnen
silhouette_score <- function(k){
  km <- kmeans(df, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  ss <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(df))
  mean(ss[, 3])
}

k_values <- 2:10
avg_sil <- sapply(k_values, silhouette_score)

# Plot zur Auswahl des besten k
plot(k_values, avg_sil, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Anzahl der Cluster (k)",
     ylab = "Durchschnittliche Silhouettenbreite",
     main = "Silhouettenanalyse zur Bestimmung der optimalen Clusteranzahl")

# Bestes k ermitteln
best_k <- k_values[which.max(avg_sil)]

# KMeans & Silhouette für bestes k
km_best <- kmeans(df, centers = best_k, nstart = 25)
sil <- silhouette(km_best$cluster, dist(df))

# Silhouettenplot anzeigen wie im Beispielbild

                main = paste("Silhouettenplot für k =", best_k))
```

#####PART 4: Linear regression
```{r}
### read Table_RBPs

# read table
raw <- readLines("data/Table_HS_RBP.txt")
# extract everything below row 7
raw_data <- raw[7:length(raw)]

# clean the table
clean_data <- gsub('\\"', '', raw_data)
writeLines(clean_data, "cleaned_table.txt")
Table_HS_RBP = read.delim("cleaned_table.txt",
                    sep = "\t",
                    header = TRUE,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                    check.names = FALSE)
head(Table_HS_RBP)

```


```{r}
# read Table_Non_RBP


# whole table
raw <- readLines("data/Table_HS_Non_RBP.txt")
# extract everything below row 7
raw_data <- raw[7:length(raw)]

# clean the table 
clean_data <- gsub('\\"', '', raw_data)
writeLines(clean_data, "cleaned_table.txt")
Table_HS_Non_RBP = read.delim("cleaned_table.txt",
                    sep = "\t",
                    header = TRUE,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                    check.names = FALSE)
head(Table_HS_Non_RBP)

```


```{r}
# check if all our proteins are included in the tables 
all_proteins <- test_scores_combined_df$Protein
proteins_rbp <- Table_HS_RBP$Entry_Name
proteins_non_rbp <- Table_HS_Non_RBP$Entry_Name

is_in_rbp_or_nonrbp <- test_scores_combined_df %in% proteins_rbp | test_scores_combined_df %in% proteins_non_rbp

all(is_in_rbp_or_nonrbp)#

```


```{r}
# 1. Nur relevante Spalten aus RBP- und Non-RBP-Tabellen auswählen
rbp_subset <- Table_HS_RBP[, c("Entry_Name", "pI", "Mass_kDa" , "Length_AA")]
non_rbp_subset <- Table_HS_Non_RBP[, c("Entry_Name", "pI", "Mass_kDa", "Length_AA")]

# 2. Zusammenführen beider Tabellen
Table_HS_Combined <- rbind(rbp_subset, non_rbp_subset)

# 3. Merge: Proteinname-Spalten heißen unterschiedlich -> by.x / by.y verwenden
merged_df <- merge(test_scores_combined_df, Table_HS_Combined,
                   by.x = "Protein", by.y = "Entry_Name",
                   all.x = TRUE)  # alle aus test_scores_combined_df behalten

head(merged_df)
dim(merged_df)
```

```{r}

# Nur Zeilen ohne fehlende Werte für pI, Mass_kDa und testscores
df_complete <- merged_df[complete.cases(merged_df[, c("probability", "pI", "Mass_kDa")]), ]
# which parameters can be used in multiple regression: correlation between independent variables should be as low as possible

cor(df_complete$Mass_kDa, df_complete$pI, method = "pearson")
cor(df_complete$Mass_kDa, df_complete$Length_AA, method = "pearson")
cor(df_complete$pI, df_complete$Length_AA, method = "pearson")

# pI can be used as independent variable with either mass or length
# mass and length should not both be used due to high correlation -> we chose mass as it is experimentally more accessable than length
```


```{r}


# Regression: testscores ~ pI + Mass_kDa
model <- lm(probability ~ pI + Mass_kDa, data = df_complete)

summary(model)

```


```{r}

# visualization of linear regression using hyperplanes

install.packages("scatterplot3d") 
library(scatterplot3d)


depth <- df_complete$probability

# Farbverlauf: dunkel-lila -> mittleres Lila -> helles Lila
farben <- colorRampPalette(c("#b19cd9", "#7b59b9", "#4b0082"))(100)

color_index <- cut(depth, breaks = 100, labels = FALSE)
point_colors <- farben[color_index]

s3d <- scatterplot3d(df_complete$pI, df_complete$Mass_kDa, df_complete$probability,
                     xlab = "pI", ylab = "Masse (kDa)", zlab = "Probability",
                     pch = 16, color = point_colors,
                     highlight.3d = FALSE,
                     type = "p", angle = 55)

s3d$plane3d(model, col = "#4b0082")



# Koordinaten der Regressionsfläche berechnen
plane <- predict(model, 
                 newdata = data.frame(pI = df_complete$pI, 
                                      Mass_kDa = df_complete$Mass_kDa))

# Fläche einzeichnen
s3d$plane3d(model)
```

```{r}
# create interactive hyperplane 


install.packages("plotly")
library(plotly)

# new classification
df_complete$RBP_shift_category <- ifelse(df_complete$probability >= optimal_threshold,
                                         ifelse(df_complete$Shift_direction_ctrl_to_rnase == "left shift", "RBP_left",
                                                ifelse(df_complete$Shift_direction_ctrl_to_rnase == "right shift", "RBP_right", "RBP")),
                                         "Non-RBP")


# grid for regressionplane
pI_seq <- seq(min(df_complete$pI), max(df_complete$pI), length.out = 30)
Mass_seq <- seq(min(df_complete$Mass_kDa), max(df_complete$Mass_kDa), length.out = 30)
grid <- expand.grid(pI = pI_seq, Mass_kDa = Mass_seq)
grid$predicted <- predict(model, newdata = grid)

# determine colors
farben <- list("RBP_left" = "#c9a0dc",     # hell-lila
               "RBP_right" = "#7a42a6",    # dunkel-lila
               "RBP" = "purple",
               "Non-RBP" = "lightgray")

# Plotly Plot 
fig <- plot_ly()

# RBP_left
fig <- fig %>%
  add_markers(data = subset(df_complete, RBP_shift_category == "RBP_left"),
              x = ~pI, y = ~Mass_kDa, z = ~probability,
              marker = list(color = farben[["RBP_left"]], size = 4),
              name = "RBP (left shift)")

# RBP_right
fig <- fig %>%
  add_markers(data = subset(df_complete, RBP_shift_category == "RBP_right"),
              x = ~pI, y = ~Mass_kDa, z = ~probability,
              marker = list(color = farben[["RBP_right"]], size = 4),
              name = "RBP (right shift)")

# RBP without Shift-Direction 
fig <- fig %>%
  add_markers(data = subset(df_complete, RBP_shift_category == "RBP"),
              x = ~pI, y = ~Mass_kDa, z = ~probability,
              marker = list(color = farben[["RBP"]], size = 4),
              name = "RBP (no shift info)")

# Non-RBP
fig <- fig %>%
  add_markers(data = subset(df_complete, RBP_shift_category == "Non-RBP"),
              x = ~pI, y = ~Mass_kDa, z = ~probability,
              marker = list(color = farben[["Non-RBP"]], size = 4),
              name = "Non-RBP")

# Regressionplane
fig <- fig %>%
  add_surface(x = ~pI_seq,
              y = ~Mass_seq,
              z = matrix(grid$predicted, nrow = 30),
              opacity = 0.5,
              colorscale = "Purples",
              showscale = FALSE,
              name = "Regression Surface")

# Layout
fig <- fig %>%
  layout(scene = list(
    xaxis = list(title = "pI"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Mass (kDa)", tick0 = 0, dtick = 100, range = c(0, 1000)),
    zaxis = list(title = "Probability")
  ),
  legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Protein Classification</b>")))

fig


```

```{r}


#hypothesis: proteins with a higher pI are more significantly more likely to be RBPs -> have positively charged domains at physiological pH -> are more likely to bind negatively charged RNA

# Group proteins based on optimal threshold:
df_complete$RBP_group <- ifelse(df_complete$probability > optimal_threshold,
                               "RBP", "Non-RBP")

# Optional: check mean pI values per group to confirm
aggregate(pI ~ RBP_group, data = df_complete, mean)

# Perform one-sided Welch Two Sample t-test comparing pI of RBP vs Non-RBP
# as big sample sizes are used, it was assumed that the central limit theorem applies (meaning the data follows a normal distribution)
t_test_result <- t.test(
  df_complete$pI[df_complete$RBP_group == "RBP"],
  df_complete$pI[df_complete$RBP_group == "Non-RBP"],
  alternative = "greater"
)

print(t_test_result)

```

```{r}


#check whether mass differs significantly between RBPs and Non-RBPs

# Perform two-sided Welch Two Sample t-test comparing pI of RBP vs Non-RBP
t_test_result <- t.test(
  df_complete$Mass_kDa[df_complete$RBP_group == "RBP"],
  df_complete$Mass_kDa[df_complete$RBP_group == "Non-RBP"],
)

print(t_test_result)
```

```{r}


# create boxplot
boxplot(pI ~ RBP_group,
        data = df_complete,
        col = c("lightblue", "lavender"),
        main = "compare pI\nbetween RBP and Non-RBP",
        xlab = "group",
        ylab = "isoelectric point (pI)")

# calculate mean
mean_rbp <- mean(df_complete$pI[df_complete$RBP_group == "RBP"])
mean_nonrbp <- mean(df_complete$pI[df_complete$RBP_group == "Non-RBP"])

print(mean_rbp)
print(mean_nonrbp)

# depict mean in plot
points(c(1, 2), c(mean_nonrbp, mean_rbp), pch = 19, col = "coral")

# Oadd legend
legend("topright", legend = c("Mean"), col = "coral", pch = 19)

```

```{r}
Ctrl_data <- as.data.frame(Ctrl_pca$x)
Ctrl_data$cluster <- as.factor(C_kmeans_result$cluster)

#protein namen isolieren 
Ctrl_data$protein_name <- rownames(Ctrl_data)
#check if rbp present 
Ctrl_data$is_rbp <- Ctrl_data$protein_name %in% rbp_proteins

#farbe 
Ctrl_data$color_group <- ifelse(Ctrl_data$is_rbp, "RBP", as.character(Ctrl_data$cluster))

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(Ctrl_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = color_group, shape = is_rbp)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  labs(title = "K-Means Cluster im PCA-Raum",
       x = "Hauptkomponente 1 (PC1)",
       y = "Hauptkomponente 2 (PC2)",
       color = "Gruppe",
       shape = "Protein-Typ") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 17)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("1" = "blue", "2" = "light grey", "RBP" = "purple"))


ggplot(Ctrl_data,aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = cluster, shape = rbp_label)) +
  
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("non-RBP" = 16, "RBP" = 17)) +
  labs(shape = "Protein-Typ")
```
